sections.title: 3c. Subagent dispatch discipline
sections.summary: Background dispatch never blocks the main session; the model and thinking level come from `.env.local`, are used as dispatch parameters only, and are never printed or committed.
sections.source: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (subagent dispatch discipline)

rules.text: After dispatching you must register the executor (a **self-declared ledger**, not identity proof): `config.set executor.<rN>.<stage>=<agent_id>`, live stage ∈ plan / development (analysis is a legacy compatibility slot only — never a live stage, never registered for new work); when one subagent covers both live stages, register the same id stage by stage. Replacing the executor for the same (req, stage) with a different id **requires** a reason (`=<new_id>|<reason>`); a **cross-stage handoff** (a development id different from the plan id) equally requires a reason and may never be silently overwritten as a "first binding for that stage". A successful handoff writes `id|reason` and appends one entry to `req.<i>.hist` (reusing the rolling cap; no separate history/handoff key); a clean first binding writes no history. The ledger carries no rev: `amend` does not change the binding and `split` / `merge` do not inherit it. `proposal.submit` performs no hard check — an unregistered executor only shows as "unregistered" in `requirement.list` and never blocks external proposals or same-ext replays.
rules.basis: user decision 2026-11-01 (E2 ruling: reuse config.set, bind no rev, no hard submit gate, a cross-stage handoff must give a reason)

rules.text: A genuinely new architectural decision gets its `D-MAx` number allocated serially by the main session at dispatch time and written into the requirement description and the subagent brief; an existing decision reuses its existing number. An executor never self-allocates `max+1`: two lanes picking `max+1` from the same base double-claimed `D-MA16` (see docs/CONTEXT.md history `d0b4a7c` / `6848138`). IDs beyond the brief are not self-served — return to the coordinator.
rules.basis: user decision 2026-11-12 (E9: parallel-lane D-MA16 collision)

rules.text: Every subagent task runs in the background; the main session never waits in place — keep advancing other lanes, verifications or planning while it runs, and verify and merge once the completion notice arrives.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (dispatch discipline 1)

rules.text: Synchronous waiting is allowed only when the next action strictly depends on the result and nothing else can progress in parallel; even then, spend the waiting time on other lanes first.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (dispatch discipline 1)

rules.text: Before dispatching, **must `source .env.local`** (the repository-root, git-ignored, never committed) to load the environment variables (git-ignored, never committed): `YGG_SUBAGENT_MODEL` (the subagent model, e.g. `sonnet` / `provider/model-id`) and `YGG_SUBAGENT_THINKING` (`off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max`); when unset, pass nothing explicitly and use the harness default.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (dispatch discipline 2)

rules.text: These two values are dispatch parameters only — never printed, never written into documentation, never committed.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (dispatch discipline 2)

rules.text: Runtime projection of `docs/design/identity.md`: submit with `exec=<agent_id>` and the declared actor environment, and register the profile card one key per `config.set`. The host-owned actor segments and three-state cross-check recognise rather than reject; forged actor segments are refused, while an unverified proxy remains visibly unverified.
rules.basis: docs/design/identity.md (runtime projection)

sections.title: 4. Develop → integrate → merge → deploy
sections.summary: Three closing levels: the iteration point (feature → develop, executed by the requirement's development executor inside its own lane at closeout) → the round (develop → master, executed by the main agent — human-triggered under guide, agent-triggered under goal) → deployment; iteration-level integration never lags behind a completed requirement and is never batched at round closeout.

rules.text: Iteration-level integration (feature → develop) is executed by the requirement's development executor inside its own lane at closeout — the main agent never performs an iteration-level integration. Integration serializes per repo through `origin/develop` itself: re-align before merging; a rejected develop push means another lane landed first — re-align and retry; stacked lanes integrate base-first. Round-level (develop → master) and deployment remain serial main-agent duties.
rules.basis: user decision (D-MA22): executor integrates feature→develop, main flow only develop→master

rules.text: First step of an iteration closeout: `git fetch origin`.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (1)

rules.text: All gates must be green on the feature branch itself before integration starts (see the gates chapter) — this admission check is purely branch-local evidence, and it never carries over: after the feature lands in `develop` the integrated state is tested again (`integration.iter.test-after-integrate`).
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (1)

rules.text: Before rebasing, check that local `develop` and `origin/develop` have not diverged: if they have diverged, stop, analyse and report to the user instead of resolving it automatically; otherwise `git pull origin develop --ff-only`.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Rebase the feature branch onto the local `develop` — this is the standing path for every requirement closeout, not an exception.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: When the rebase conflicts, stop the whole-branch rebase and replay commit by commit with `git cherry-pick`; land each conflict as its own standalone conflict-resolution commit so every step stays auditable.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: After any history rewrite (rebase or cherry-pick replay), push with `git push --force-with-lease origin <feature>`; a bare push is forbidden.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Integration runs inside the executor's own lane workspace, never the main checkout: `git fetch origin`, align local `develop` with `origin/develop` (`--ff-only`), merge the local feature ref with `git merge --no-ff <feature>`, then push `develop`; deleting the remote feature branch stays optional.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Never merge `origin/feature/*`: after a rebase the remote ref still points at the old head, so merging it fabricates duplicate same-content commits plus an orphaned merge node — merge only the local ref.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: The executor proves the integrated state inside the integration worktree before pushing `develop`: the feature-branch admission green never carries over — an iteration point closes on integrated-state evidence.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Pushing the feature branch alone is not a closeout: a requirement closes only after it is merged into `develop` and proven on the integrated state — the acceptance artifacts must carry the develop merge SHA (`develop@<sha>`) as integration evidence, and `develop` must never lag behind a completed requirement.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: A round-level closeout first passes end-to-end acceptance on the `develop` integrated state once every in-round feature has landed: the example game completed end to end plus save/load verification; after M1 this adds the AI-generated → playable loop — the precondition for merging into `master`.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (2)

rules.text: Integration and the `master` merge are two separate stages and never execute as one: while any in-round feature has not landed in `develop` yet, merging into `master` is forbidden.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: The `develop` → `master` merge is a normal round-closeout step; the trigger follows `play.mode` — under `guide` the human approves it through the gate ticket, under `goal` the main agent executes it as part of its dispatch authority. The ritual itself is identical: `git fetch origin`, then divergence-check `master` and `develop` separately and align each with `--ff-only`, then in the main checkout `git merge --no-ff develop`, then `git push origin master` — the merge is not complete until the trunk is pushed; rebasing `develop` is absolutely forbidden — the merge topology is the rollback history.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: `develop` syncs to `master` exclusively by reset — after the round merge, and equally after any direct master commit (hotfixes, standalone fixes): `git reset --hard master` on `develop` so `develop` equals `master` as the clean baseline for the next round, then `git push --force-with-lease origin develop`. Merging `master` into `develop` (a reverse merge) is forbidden: it pollutes develop's topology with merge edges against the designed flow feature → develop → master and duplicates master content as meaningless merge nodes.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Once acceptance passes, tag the batch `v<YYYY.MM.DD>.<n>` — the no-FF merge node is the rollback anchor.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (2)

rules.text: A batch closeout updates the CHANGELOG / report when one exists.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (2)

rules.text: Anything deployed through any channel must already be merged into master: a non-master ref is refused outright, with no exception switch.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (3)

rules.text: Deployment is a write operation: report it to the user and get approval before every deployment.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (3)

sections.title: 5. Verification-command gates
sections.summary: The gate baseline is a snapshot: the acceptance standard is "introduce no new failure"; a module whose gate is not wired up must be declared uncovered explicitly.

rules.text: The gate baseline is a snapshot that grows with each iteration, and the acceptance standard is "introduce no new failure" — historical debt does not have to be zero, but no new failure may appear.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history)

rules.text: Runtime projection of `docs/design/state-machine.md` §2.11: three-suite green is claimed only by running `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --example egg -p ygg-sandbox`, and `cargo test -p ygg-sandbox --test agent_seed_semantics` verbatim and recording each real exit code and test count. `cargo check`, filtered or single-test runs, `verify-suite --mode fast`, and `YGG_VERIFY_COMMANDS` overrides are evidence of the substitute only; using one as the literal gate is a fake green.
rules.basis: docs/design/state-machine.md §2.11 (runtime projection); user decision 2026-11-12 (E7)

rules.text: The dependency list in `ygg-core`'s `Cargo.toml` is part of the review: a rendering, platform or IO dependency is a violation with no exception mechanism.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (kernel purity check)

rules.text: A module whose gate is not wired up yet (no tests exist) must be declared "gate not covered" in the report; it never passes by default.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history)

rules.text: Runtime projection of `docs/design/state-machine.md` §2.10: changing `.ygg/mods/agent-seed/src/**`, `mod.lua`, or map wording in `data/texts/` requires `cargo test -p ygg-sandbox --test agent_seed_semantics` in addition to lint and playtest. The all-1 playtest covers only the happy path and cannot prove reject/amend/turn-cut branches; `/tmp` probes supplement rather than replace the suite, every uncovered scenario must be declared, and a mutation probe must turn the relevant assertion red. Case counts come from the real command output, never a hard-coded prompt number.
rules.basis: docs/design/state-machine.md §2.10 (runtime projection); crates/ygg-sandbox/tests/agent_seed_semantics.rs

rules.text: Never build the wasm bindings with wasm-pack: the exception-handling module needs `wasm-bindgen --reference-types` and wasm-pack does not pass that flag through; the build chain is fixed to `scripts/build-wasm.sh` (cargo plus the wasm-bindgen CLI, two steps).
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (wasm binding note); .cargo/config.toml header note

rules.text: When the FR-9 dual-run state hashes differ, never silently edit the fixture baseline — a mismatch is a determinism breach between platforms, and a baseline change requires an explicit decision plus a record.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (FR-9 note)

rules.text: Before claiming full FR-9 compliance, add the wasm-bindgen-test browser lane (replay the same assertions in a real browser wasm instance) or take an explicit waiver decision; today the node lane covers native/wasm dual-run equivalence, and the browser lane does not exist.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (FR-9 residual-gap note)

rules.text: Contract parity criterion: the same Mod sample must produce identical results through ajv and through the jsonschema crate; the CI script does not exist yet, so until it lands that surface is declared "gate not covered".
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (contract parity)
